clue.text: Video of nun wandering around Portugal essentially wasting cardinal's money

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the piece for Portugal
letters that wander roam from their places, so the video-of-nun letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter of wasting is used

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four cardinal points of the compass

explanation.surface: A spendthrift cardinal blows his cash on a film about a nun roaming around Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges VIDEOOFNUN to FIVEOUNDNO; 'around' puts it round P. 'essentially' takes T, the middle of wasting, and 'cardinal' is not a churchman but E, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pound note is a British banknote, so it is a piece of paper currency.

clue.text: Temperature in Fahrenheit on day before beginning of Ramadan

parts.note: an eve is the day before a festival or event

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of Ramadan

explanation.surface: A weather report: it is hot on the day before Ramadan starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fever is a raised body temperature, as in 'running a temperature'.

clue.text: Tribesman detailed to guard queen covered entrance

indicators.note: the shortened word surrounds the queen as guards would
de-tailed: the word for tribesman loses its tail, its last letter

parts.note: a Vandal was a member of the Germanic tribe that sacked Rome
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A warrior is detailed to stand guard over the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'assigned' but means de-tailed, leaving VANDA; 'to guard' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed porch or gallery along the outside of a house, a sheltered way in.

clue.text: Papa, having lost wife, cries buckets

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: having lost something means doing without it, so a letter is dropped from the word for cries

parts.note: wails are loud cries of grief

explanation.surface: A widowed father weeps buckets, crying copiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cries buckets' reads as one idiom for weeping hard, but 'buckets' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Pails are open containers with handles, the same thing as buckets.

clue.text: Peacekeepers seal off hospital for free

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces are sent by the United Nations

indicators.note: off in the sense of wrong or awry, so the letters of seal are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: United Nations troops cordon off a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal off' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'off' scrambles SEAL into LEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to let loose or release, as a dog is freed from its lead.

clue.text: Students record independent album about hollow experiences

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: about as in turned about, so the album's letters are read backwards

parts.note: an LP, long-player, is an album

indicators.note: a hollow word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Students release an indie record about empty experiences.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'on' gives no reversal; the setter's 'about' turned LP to PL, an editing error the setter confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Disciples are followers who learn from a teacher, so pupils or students.

clue.text: See 1
Conquerors of Poles hoisting standard on top of arsenal

indicators.note: in a down entry the poles sit underneath and lift up what is above them

parts.note: a norm is a standard or usual level

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, here of arsenal

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish soldiers raise their flag over a captured armoury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the letters N and S, which 'hoisting' places under NORM + A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans under William conquered England in 1066.

clue.text: Attempt to hide protective gear commandeered by terrorists in Irish town

indicators.note: the word for attempt surrounds the rest, hiding it from view

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: something commandeered is seized and held, so the terrorists enclose the gear

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, carried out a terrorist campaign
PPE stands for personal protective equipment

explanation.surface: Terrorists in an Irish town hijack a shipment of protective equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested insertions: 'commandeered by' makes IPPERA, and 'to hide' wraps the attempt around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is a town in Ireland, famous from the wartime song about the long way there.

clue.text: Frenzied attack upon retired clergyman opening fair? Sick!

indicators.note: the clergyman's letters open up the word for fair and sit inside it

parts.note: OK means fair or passable

indicators.note: retired as in withdrawn, going back, so the word for clergyman runs backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman's title
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A shocked report of a vicious assault on an elderly vicar at a village fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns REV into VER, which goes into OK. 'clergyman opening fair' suggests a vicar declaring a fête open.
explanation.definitionFit: Overkill is excessive force, more than is needed; a frenzied attack goes far beyond what is necessary.

clue.text: Writing exercise follows extremely schematic lesson

indicators.note: the exercise comes after the other pieces
taking a word at its extremes means using only its first and last letters

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, is a school lesson
PT, physical training, is exercise

explanation.surface: A teacher sets a writing exercise after a very diagrammatic lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writing exercise' looks like one phrase, but 'Writing' alone is the definition and 'exercise' is PT.
explanation.definitionFit: Script is handwriting, or the written text of a play or film.

clue.text: Advertising is about trust in impressions

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity work akin to advertising

indicators.note: the word is goes around the trust's letters

parts.note: the NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Advertising relies on trust to shape public impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressions' looks like opinions, but here it means marks pressed into something. The National Trust is a British charity looking after historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: Prints are marks left by pressure, as fingerprints or footprints are impressions.

clue.text: A twisted jibe about gallery in troubled state

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the gallery
twisted round, so the word for jibe is read backwards

parts.note: a dig is a sly jibe
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A cruel jibe made about an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' reverses DIG to GID, which goes 'about' TATE. The Tate is London's famous group of art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated describes someone anxious and stirred up, in a troubled state of mind.

clue.text: Salvation Army quarters behind home for mentally disturbed

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the word for home

parts.note: in means at home
N and E, north and east, are two quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Salvation Army living quarters behind a home for the mentally ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests lodgings but means the compass points N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Insane means suffering from serious mental illness, a now-dated word for disturbed.

clue.text: Entire FT spread about India's royal consort

indicators.note: letters spread about are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The whole Financial Times covers India's royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread about' rearranges the letters to NEFERTIT. FT is the Financial Times, where the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was the queen and great royal wife of the Egyptian pharaoh Akhenaten.

clue.text: CIA handle criminal's fare from Mexico

indicators.note: criminal as in an outrageous mess, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The CIA dealing with a Mexican criminal's business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like a ticket price but means food.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a tortilla rolled round a filling and baked in sauce.

clue.text: Exert power over husband and son by traditional method

indicators.note: by means beside, so the son's letter sits next to the word for traditional

parts.note: old means traditional, long-established
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A patriarch rules over husband and son in the old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter explained that 'by' just means beside, on either side, so the son may follow 'traditional' rather than precede it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to have power or control, as a ruler or dominant influence.

clue.text: Wrongdoings of church in parts of Eastern England

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is set inside the word for the region

parts.note: the Fens are the flat marshland of East Anglia in eastern England
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A report on the church's misdeeds in rural East Anglia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are a low-lying, drained marshland region of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Offences are crimes or breaches of law, so wrongdoings.

clue.text: Regularly tells mate about English timber supplier

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following words

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone keeps telling a friend about English wood suppliers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'tells mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elm is a tree whose wood is used as timber, so the tree is a source of wood.

clue.text: Hang from post outside American battleship's base

indicators.note: the word for post goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
US means American

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of a word is its bottom, last letter

explanation.surface: A sailor is to be hanged from a post outside a US naval base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battleship's base' sounds like a naval base, but it is the last letter of 'battleship'.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above.

clue.text: Wanders off and runs into reinforcements

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the word for reinforcements

parts.note: stays are supports, such as the stiffening strips in a corset or ropes bracing a mast
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A soldier deserts and runs into the reinforcements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' fits the flight picture but is just R; 'reinforcements' are not troops but supports.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to roam away from the right place, so strays means wanders off.

clue.text: Take retaliatory action regarding South Atlantic

parts.note: re means regarding
the Pond is a jocular name for the Atlantic Ocean

explanation.surface: A call for reprisals in the South Atlantic, as in the Falklands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Pond' is a humorous British and American name for the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond can mean to react to an attack by hitting back.

clue.text: Men wrestling with girl's problems

indicators.note: letters that wrestle tumble about and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: Men grappling with a girlfriend's troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins: 'wrestling' rearranges MEN and GIRLS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Gremlins are imaginary imps blamed for unexplained faults, so mechanical problems or glitches.

clue.text: Drunk starts to lecture youth in an extravagant manner

parts.note: a lush is a heavy drinker

indicators.note: the starts of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A drunk begins to lecture a young person, waving his arms about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as an adjective but is the noun LUSH, a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lushly means luxuriously or richly, done lavishly.

clue.text: Lose one's faith in large part of church structure

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the apse is the rounded recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: Losing faith while sitting in a large church.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapsed believer is one who has stopped practising their religion.

clue.text: In general, IT headhunter is flexible

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: An IT recruitment consultant is generally adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'generally', but 'In' marks the letters inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and bending easily, as a gymnast is.

clue.text: Mountainous region in South Africa one's entered by mistake

indicators.note: the other pieces sit inside the abbreviation for South Africa
the numeral is followed in by the word for mistake

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone has strayed into the mountains of South Africa by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged mountain range, as in the Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Adventures of former international included in storylines

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the word for storylines

parts.note: plots are storylines

explanation.surface: A former international footballer's adventures feature in tabloid storylines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former international' reads as a retired player, but EX and I are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploits are daring deeds or adventures.

clue.text: Obstacle circumvented by rogue in Evil Dead movie

indicators.note: circumvented means surrounded, so the rearranged letters go around the obstacle
rogue as in wayward, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A rogue gets round an obstacle in a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' makes LIVEANDDIE, which 'circumvented by' wraps around the obstacle. 'Evil Dead' is a real horror film, a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Live and Let Die is the 1973 James Bond film.
